title: Verified settlement projection accepts a different queue request under the same operation ID

evidence.observed: A real fully validated fixture PrivateLedger is matched to a supported offline pending Queue by operation_id only. Different request hashes still yield captured + billing_verified true, with the queue hash stamped onto the ledger response. Correct-hash control passes. No database tampering.
evidence.scope: Settlement/import/recovery boundary. Normal verified dispatch separately checks request hash; no proof that it can dispatch the wrong request.

impact: A recovered queue can falsely attribute paid/verified evidence to a different request, affecting later comparisons and graph provenance despite an intact payer ledger.

alternatives.name: Reject mismatched imported rows before projection
Explicit audited legacy mapping proves operation/request/route/manifest and settlement identity
alternatives.status: representable; not implemented at this boundary

target_data_graph_object: Queue job -> immutable payer attempt -> exact request/response witness -> method_run/result provenance

acceptance_test.expected: Reject request mismatch, remain pending, retain no result or settlement evidence, never resend. Preserve the valid control C2-PAYER-01 and verified bridge native roundtrip C2-NATIVE-02.

migration: Preserve original payer receipts. Quarantine legacy queues lacking exact request association; require explicit checked mapping instead of relabeling results or retrying transport.
migration_risk: Historical captured results may already contain the queue hash rather than payer hash; blindly trusting those records preserves false attribution.
dependencies: C owns research boundary; B owns product integration
Resolve before using recovered research results as production profile evidence

title: New public handoff entrypoint does not restrict auxiliary protocol/projection fields

evidence.observed: Synthetic unknown auxiliary object in protocol or projection is emitted and recoverable as policy or projection-profile-bytes. Presentation-only schema validation does not cover these auxiliary sources. Existing frozen public artifact has not been shown to contain private content.

impact: A future mistaken private annotation placed in a public-build auxiliary input is preserved in the public packet, including source-byte fields.

alternatives.name: Versioned strict public projection contract over all contributing sources
Explicit reviewed public references with private bytes excluded
alternatives.status: existing graph mechanism supports references; wrapper policy not demonstrated

target_data_graph_object: Public artifact projection policy; source visibility/provenance and source-byte inclusion decisions

acceptance_test.expected: Unexpected auxiliary data is rejected with a safe diagnostic or excluded by an explicit public projection before any packet/source emission; preserve legitimate exact recovery of approved public bytes.

migration: Do not rewrite historical seals. Introduce a reviewed public wrapper/schema version and explicitly classify all captured sources. Generic graph exporter remains a byte-preserving mechanism.
migration_risk: Overly broad stripping loses provenance; only the public projection should select visibility, while reviewed private artifacts retain full data.
dependencies: C public preparation wrapper; B must not treat generic GraphPacket validation as privacy validation

title: Public presentation rejection exposes rejected input through the uncaught CLI exception

evidence.observed: Schema rejects an unknown presentation field and emits no artifact, but ValidationError string and standard Python sys.excepthook output contain the synthetic input canary. Runner captures this only in memory and publishes hashes/status.

impact: Diagnostic logs from an unsuccessful public artifact build can expose input even when the artifact gate correctly rejects it.

alternatives.name: Fixed public diagnostic code and field path, no rejected value
Detailed errors retained only in explicitly private receipt
alternatives.status: optional strategy; not implemented by public CLI

target_data_graph_object: Public build error event with safe machine code; optional private diagnostic evidence reference

acceptance_test.expected: Reject malformed presentation before output; no canary in public exception, stdout, stderr, or artifact; maintain valid-build C2-PUBLIC-01.

migration: No data migration; keep original private diagnostics private and avoid attaching historical raw exception logs to public reports.
migration_risk: Suppressing every error would impair debugging; preserve stable error code and safe path while withholding input values.
dependencies: C public CLI or B wrapper error handler
R42 exception 6 permits diagnostics, not disclosure of private inputs
